bisect.name: Reversal tracing
bisect.why: Binary search through tri-temporal history: “from when did my stance on X change?”. A tool for epistemic meta-reflection.
bisect.baseTask: Implement the bisect operation in layer C5: select two atoms (good/bad) on the same concept, and the system proposes the pivot atoms to examine by dichotomy.

1.label: Manual
1.desc: Bisect UI: manual chronological navigation through the tri-temporal history.

2.label: AI-assisted
2.desc: The agent proposes candidate pivots; you validate at each step.

3.label: Automatic
3.desc: The agent runs the bisect end to end and hands you the pivot atom directly.

reversal.name: Tamper-proof memory
reversal.why: Never an in-place UPDATE: to correct an atom, you create a `reversal` atom that explicitly inverts it plus a corrected atom. Integrity guaranteed by construction, not by control.
reversal.baseTask: Add the `reversal` type to the frontmatter + a cryptographic signature on the reversal atom + a default filter in the orchestrator.

1.label: Logical
1.desc: `reversal` type in the frontmatter, without a crypto signature. Append-only by convention.

2.label: HMAC-signed
2.desc: `reversal` type + HMAC signature over (original_atom_id, content_hash, timestamp). Append-only guaranteed.

3.label: Chained ledger
3.desc: HMAC + chained hash of every atom (blockchain-style). Full ledger integrity.

prereg.name: Time-stamped decisions
prereg.why: State the hypothesis + success criterion BEFORE the decision. The postmortem must reference the pre-registration. Structural defence against confirmation bias.
prereg.baseTask: Add a `pre_reg` type to the schema + a decision → postmortem workflow that references it.

1.label: Soft
1.desc: Pre-registration optional, merely recommended in the docs.

2.label: Linked
2.desc: The postmortem may reference a parent pre-registration (non-blocking).

3.label: Hard
3.desc: Pre-registration mandatory and blocking before any structuring decision. The postmortem must resolve it.

mel.name: Failure plan
mel.why: Pre-thought doctrine: “what can be down while the agent still works, with repair time and an alternative procedure”. Not improvised during an incident.
mel.baseTask: Write the MEL: a matrix of components × failure types × maximum delay × alternative procedure.

1.label: Draft
1.desc: MEL written for critical components only.

2.label: Tested
2.desc: MEL + degradation tests once per component (verifies the degraded mode works).

3.label: Monitored
3.desc: MEL + tests + automatic monitoring that detects the failure and switches to degraded mode.

4.label: Certified
4.desc: MEL + regular tests + audit trail + annual review of the matrix.

conflict.name: Conflict detector
conflict.why: Before an atom touches a client/project/entity, an automatic cross-reference: “is this entity an adversary / competitor / target of another decision?”. Prevents contradictory advice.
conflict.baseTask: NER (spaCy or local Gliner) on ingestion + an entity index + a pre-query check in the orchestrator.

1.label: Basic NER
1.desc: Named-entity extraction (spaCy / Gliner). Alert on exact match.

2.label: NER + graph
2.desc: Entity graph + fuzzy-match detection (spelling variants, aliases).

3.label: + temporal
3.desc: Check on the bitemporal axis: “was this entity in a different context before?”

4.label: + cross-circle
4.desc: Check across every circle (active multi-tenancy). Cross-client alert.

compliance.rgpdAipd: 📄 Draft a DPIA (Data Protection Impact Assessment)
compliance.rgpdDpa: 📋 Map your sub-processors (LLM API, host, vector DB) and sign a GDPR Art. 28 DPA with each
compliance.rgpdRegistry: 📚 Keep your GDPR Art. 30 record of processing up to date (activities + purposes)
compliance.rgpdPrivacyPolicy: 📜 Update your privacy policy (AI processing + memory base)
compliance.cndpDeclaration: 🇲🇦 File a CNDP declaration (Morocco Law 09-08), form F211 via cndp.ma
compliance.cndpRights: 📞 Document access and rectification rights (Art. 7-8, Law 09-08), 10-day SLA minimum
compliance.aiactClassify: 🤖 Classify the AI system under the AI Act: limited risk (transparency) or high risk (Art. 9-15)
compliance.aiactDeployer: ✅ If you are a deployer (Art. 26-29): complete the conformity checklist
compliance.aiactHighRisk: 📢 If high risk: risk management + human oversight + cybersecurity + automatic logging
compliance.hipaaBaa: 🇺🇸 Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with every sub-processor that handles PHI
compliance.hipaaEncryption: 🔐 AES-256 encryption at rest AND in transit, immutable audit log
compliance.secretProRls: 🔒 Lock access with Postgres RLS (“circle” field); each client matter is its own circle
compliance.secretProAnonymization: 👤 k-anonymity (k=5 minimum) on any export beyond the matter’s scope
compliance.banProprietaryMemory: 🚫 Ban vendors’ proprietary memory (ChatGPT/Claude Memory) for any structural decision
compliance.lgpdDpo: 🇧🇷 Appoint a Data Protection Officer (encarregado) — point of contact for the ANPD and data subjects (LGPD Art. 41)
compliance.lgpdRights: 📞 Operationalise data subject rights: confirmation, access, correction, anonymisation, deletion, portability (LGPD Art. 18)
compliance.lgpdRecords: 📚 Keep records of processing operations (categories, purposes, legal bases, recipients, retention — LGPD Art. 37)
compliance.lgpdRipd: 📄 Produce a Data Protection Impact Report (RIPD) for high-risk or sensitive-data processing (LGPD Art. 38)
compliance.lgpdTransfer: 🌐 Frame international transfers: adequate-protection country or specific contractual clauses (LGPD Art. 33)
compliance.lgpdIncident: 🚨 Set up security-incident notification to the ANPD and data subjects where there is relevant risk (LGPD Art. 48)
compliance.appiPurpose: 🇯🇵 Specify and notify the purpose of use; restrict use to the stated purpose (APPI, PPC)
compliance.appiSecurity: 🔐 Implement security control measures (organisational, human, physical, technical) (APPI, PPC)
compliance.appiThirdParty: 🤝 Govern third-party provision of data (prior consent; opt-out not allowed for sensitive data) (APPI, PPC)
compliance.appiRights: 📞 Respond to individuals’ requests: disclosure, correction, deletion, suspension of use and of third-party transfer (APPI, PPC)
compliance.appiIncident: 🚨 Notify the PPC and affected individuals of a data leak (mandatory since the 2022 amendment) (APPI, PPC)
compliance.appiCrossBorder: 🌐 Frame cross-border transfers: inform the individual of the recipient country and protection measures (APPI, PPC)

risks.noTechHard: ⚠️ HARD preset with non-technical skills: needs a DevOps partner, or downscale to managed MEDIUM.
risks.auditLight: 🚨 Mandatory audit is incompatible with LIGHT (no signed audit trail). Move up to MEDIUM at least.
risks.bitemporalLight: 🚨 Mandatory bitemporality is impossible on LIGHT. Switch to MEDIUM (Postgres+AGE or Graphiti).
risks.volumeLight: ⚠️ Volume > 1 TB on LIGHT: the free tier will saturate within 1-3 months. Provision MEDIUM from the start.
risks.audioOnly: 📌 Audio only: plan a Whisper large-v3 pipeline (diarization) upstream. +50-100 €/month if self-hosting GPU.
risks.videoLight: ⚠️ Video detected but LIGHT preset: transcription + frames + video embedding burns GPU. Consider MEDIUM.
risks.marocRgpdNoCndp: 🇲🇦 Morocco zone with GDPR but no CNDP: the CNDP applies on top. Double-check.
risks.usersLight: ⚠️ {users} users on LIGHT: no strict multi-tenancy (RLS). Switch to MEDIUM (RLS + circle field).
risks.voicesLight: ⚠️ Multi-perspective on LIGHT: no governance of voices. Move to MEDIUM or V1+ soon.
risks.budgetOverflow: 💰 Budget < 50 € but estimated cost {totalCost} €: over by {over} €. Reduce scope or raise the budget.
risks.manyContentLight: 🔄 4+ content types on LIGHT: ingestion complexity exceeds what LIGHT supports. Switch to MEDIUM.
risks.reqLight: 📈 > 10k requests/day: direct LIGHT API gets expensive. Self-hosting vLLM (MEDIUM/HARD) pays off.
risks.latencyLight: ⚡ Low latency expected but LIGHT preset (third-party managed API, no latency guarantee): move to MEDIUM (self-host to control latency).
risks.growthLight: 🌱 High growth anticipated but LIGHT: provision MEDIUM from the start to absorb the ramp-up without an emergency migration.
risks.noRegSensitive: ⚖️ No legal regime checked but non-public sensitivity: almost always a mistake (GDPR applies as soon as personal data is involved).

guidance.availability: Switch to read-only from the last valid backup; suspend new writes until service is restored.
guidance.resilience: Freeze critical writes until a valid, tested backup is confirmed.
guidance.compliance: Suspend processing of uncovered regulated data; restrict access to the strict minimum.
guidance.budget: Freeze non-essential scale-ups; operate at the current sizing.
guidance.freshness: Re-validate sourced prices and statuses before any quoted commitment; show freshness.
guidance.drift: Operate while flagging the gap; do not rely on components diverging from the recommendation for structural decisions.

corrective.availability: Restart or scale the failing services, check health-checks and capacity.
corrective.resilience: Restore and test a backup; reinstate the 3-2-1-1 policy and immutability.
corrective.compliance: Handle open compliance actions (record, DPA, rights); have a counsel validate.
corrective.budget: Review sizing and over-target items; arbitrate cost levers.
corrective.freshness: Re-run the price and legal watch; reconfirm dated sources.
corrective.drift: Realign the deployed configuration with the recommendation; document or justify the gap.

zone.why: The hosting location determines which laws apply (GDPR, CNDP) and exposure to foreign jurisdictions (Cloud Act).
zone.consequence: A non-EU zone may subject your data to foreign access rights.

regulations.why: Each regime checked adds concrete obligations (Art. 30 register, DPIA, CNDP filing…).
regulations.consequence: The matching compliance actions are listed in the recommendation.

sensitivity.why: The sensitivity level drives the required encryption, isolation and auditability.
sensitivity.consequence: The more sensitive, the more the stack hardens, and the cost rises.

techLevel.why: Your skills determine what can be run in-house, without a provider.
techLevel.consequence: A non-technical profile leans toward managed services: faster ramp-up.

budget.why: The monthly budget bounds the field of infrastructure choices (managed vs self-hosted).
budget.consequence: Any overrun against this budget is explicitly flagged.

volume.why: Data volume sizes the storage and the vector indexing.
volume.consequence: A high volume increases storage cost and may require a more robust stack.

reqPerDay.why: Request throughput sizes inference and the LLM gateway.
reqPerDay.consequence: High throughput makes self-hosting (vLLM) more economical than pay-per-call API.

voices.why: The number of perspectives drives access governance and the search combinatorics.
voices.consequence: Several voices imply audited delegation (RLS, multi-tenant).

contentTypes.why: Content types determine the embeddings model (text-only vs multimodal).
contentTypes.consequence: Multimodal (audio/video/images) adds models and GPU, detailed in the Media block.

audit.why: Signed audit traces, tamper-proof, who wrote what and when.
audit.consequence: Requiring audit rules out the lightest presets (no signed journal).

bitemporal.why: Bitemporality distinguishes “when it happened” from “when we learned it”, replaying the state of knowledge at a given date.
bitemporal.consequence: Requiring bitemporality mandates dedicated storage (Postgres+AGE, Graphiti…).

preferSovereign.why: Steers the recommendation toward a more self-hosted, open-source stack, rather than proprietary tools that lock you in.
preferSovereign.consequence: The preset is bumped up one notch (self-host components): more sovereignty, but higher cost and complexity — any tension with the budget is flagged, never hidden.

continent.why: Where your data and users live, worldwide — every continent is covered.
continent.consequence: Drives hosting and the providers proposed; you then specify the country.

country.why: The precise jurisdiction drives data-transfer analysis. Detailed for the EU, Morocco and the United States; elsewhere, a conservative default to validate with counsel.
country.consequence: Refines the local providers proposed; engineering guidance, not legal advice.

note.doneNothing: Nothing to adjust in this note; manual entry remains available.

backup.sectionDesc: Pick a criticality: the plan (RPO/RTO, copies, off-site, retention, erasure) follows from it, and expert tuning stays possible. The recurring cost feeds the budget meter.

criticalityInfo.why: Criticality derives the whole plan: backup frequency (RPO), recovery time (RTO), retention, number of copies, immutability and erasure policy.
criticalityInfo.consequence: The more critical, the more backup costs (copies, off-site, archiving), and the higher resilience climbs.

backup.noneNote: No managed backup: no extra cost, but a memory base without backup is exposed to data loss.
backup.previewDisclaimer: Variable costs ±30%, dated sources on the results page. Engineering guidance, not legal advice.

residency.sectionDesc: Where the data lives (primary jurisdiction derived from your zone) and what happens if a region goes down. You can host in several regions, including across continents. Cross-jurisdiction transfer compliance is detailed on the results page.

drInfo.why: Regional continuity decides whether memory stays available when an entire region goes down: replication to a 2nd region, failover time (RTO) and maximum loss (RPO).
drInfo.consequence: The higher the tier (warm → hot → active-active), the more a standby region and replication cost, but the faster recovery is.

regionsInfo.why: Beyond the primary jurisdiction, you can host or replicate across several regions — including across continents (finding C4).
regionsInfo.consequence: Each distinct region adds a cost (standby compute + replication) and a cross-jurisdiction flow whose compliance is assessed below.

strictInfo.why: Strict residency forbids any copy outside the primary jurisdiction (required for secrecy or certain regimes: CNDP, professional secrecy, HIPAA).
strictInfo.consequence: Under strict residency, regional continuity must stay within the same jurisdiction — a tension can arise if it does not offer 2 distinct regions.

residency.noneNote: No managed regional continuity: recovery relies on restoring the backup (no standby replica, no regional surcharge).
residency.previewPlan: Primary region “{region}” · DR {dr} · {count, plural, one {# standby region} other {# standby regions}} · RTO ≈ {rto} min.
residency.previewDisclaimer: Variable costs ±30%, dated sources on the results page. Engineering guidance, not legal advice.
